chapters.title: Temptation Is Like an Old Friend
chapters.html:
Phainon was not easily undone. He’d been shaped by silence, hardened by blood and endless solitude, his very being whittled into a blade meant for duty and nothing else. Desire was a luxury buried deep into his being long ago.

Now that Amphoreus finally knew peace, after thirty-three million agonizing cycles, he was determined to rebuild it, to shape a land where its people could breathe without fear. There was no room for indulgence, not yet. That was why he was still holding back on living for himself, there were wishes he still needed to grant before finally letting go.

That had been his selfless and totally heroic plan, until a certain gorgeously golden haired heir decided to dismantle it piece by piece, and now — now every breath felt like a fight for his life.

It began with something small. Harmless, Phainon told himself.

One morning he was resting a little from all the errands he had been running for Aglea, sprawled across the lily pads of the Garden of Life and absentmindedly playing with some Chimeras. Sunlight filtered down like molten gold as three little balls of fluff rested warmly against his tights, only a soft breeze passing through his hair.

But that peace and quiet did not last for long, because Mydei strode in imponent as ever, with that beautiful face and toned chest, sporting one damning detail that most bystanders would have missed, or at least be unbothered by (unless your name was Phainon) — a pale shade of crimson stained the prince’s mouth, the color bright and glistening against the curve of his lips. 

Phainon instantly forgot how to breathe. His brain screeched to a halt, as every survival instinct he’d ever honed in thirty-three million cycles of fly or fight abandoned him. Was he imagining things? Had all the years living beneath an eternal sun finally burned through his brain? Also, what was that? Juice? Blood? Lipstick? By the Titans, why did it look so tempting?

He couldn’t look away! The red at Mydei’s lips burned into his vision, refusing to release him.

It was no secret that Phainon had a little bit of a crush on the other man, nothing really alarming, a small weakness easily managed. Only a few people knew, probably. 

There was Castorice, who always indulged his rants. He would tell her about how Mydei had tucked a strand of hair behind his ear, or how he tilted his head like a cat when he was confused, or the way his lips tugged just a bit upwards when Phainon did something stupid. Curiously, she never complained — just nodded her head and asked him to proceed, sometimes writing some of what he said down. Again, a curious thing.

Another person who had some idea of his feelings was Hyacine, who caught him mid-stare more than once, poking his side to not be so obvious. Then Aglaea, who simply always knew everything. And finally, Cipher — who, with a grin and an unsent poem in hand, had once made him admit everything in exchange for silence. There were also some coins involved.

So yes: maybe “a crush” was generous. The truth was that even he could feel the lie in that word. What Phainon felt was not a passing fancy, no. It was a constant, bright ache that dictated his footsteps. Mydei’s casual smiles rewrote the priorities of his day, his voice smoothed the edges of the worst mornings, and the sight of golden hair in a crowd made him catch his breath like someone seeing sunlight through a storm. 

And by now everyone had already catched it. Including the man in question, it seems. 

Mydei rapidly closed the distance between them with languid confidence, armor clinking at his heels. He sank down beside Phainon without ceremony, knees brushing as he scooped a chimera into his lap. “Are you free later, Deliverer?” he began, like he didn’t have the most obscene lips in existence at that very moment. “I was planning on trying this new recipe Castorice showed me. Do you want to taste-test it, like always?” 

But Phainon couldn’t hear a damn word. Not when that mouth was moving — slow, deliberate — shaping syllables he could almost taste. Titans, those lips were too distracting. Would they feel soft under his teeth? What would they taste like? Sweet like pomegranates? Or something metallic — like iron on his tongue, a trace of enemy blood the prince hadn’t noticed remained there? That speck of crimson twisted inside him, setting his nerves on fire. He wanted — no, needed — to close in, to brush his tongue over it and make sure what it was. For research purposes, obviously.

And then Mydei dragged the tip of his tongue over his bottom lip, lazy, unthinking, catching that streak of pale red and smoothing it away. 

The world tilted as Phainon’s heart felt too large for his chest. That smear of red, the faded glint on Mydei’s lip… it flicked something awake inside him. He ached to shove the other down and lean in, to feel those lips, taste that red and have the taste of Mydei engraved so deep in him that nothing could ever take it away. But instead, he buried his fingers into the wet rim of the lily pad, the surface slick under his skin. He sucked in breath, rough and ragged, over and over — just trying to stop himself from breaking.

He looked away. He had to.

“Are you listening, Deliverer?” The words curled soft and low, far too close for comfort.

Oh right. Mydei had been speaking. That was why his mouth was moving. Those lips… irresistible… What was he talking about again? 

“Deliverer?”

He needed to say something, anything, before Mydei realized he’d been staring like a fool. He doesn't want the other thinking he wasn't paying attention!

“Yes — yes! I'll taste-test your lips for you!” The words slipped out faster than his brain could process.

Silence.

A blink. Then one eyebrow rose, elegant, smug, devastating. “You mean… my new cake recipe?”

“Cake! Right. That. Cake. Definitely cake.”

Panic flared like a battlefield fire. “Anyway! Aglaea needs me! Urgently! With… things! Important things! Good to see you, Mydeimos!”

And then like a coward, he fled, nearly tripping over his own dignity as Mydei’s laughter followed him out.

After the lipstick incident — assuming that’s what it really was on Mydei’s lips, Phainon thought he was prepared for anything, that after making a fool of himself once, nothing could surprise him anymore.

He was completely and utterly wrong.

After his pathetic exit that day, Mydei thought it would be a good idea to continue messing with his poor heart. 

The Hall of Respite was quiet in the evening,the distant hum of wind threaded through marble columns and scattered petals from the balcony’s flowerbeds everywhere. Beyond, bridges arched over yawning chasms, their paths vanishing into the mist-bound peaks of Okhema. Seated on the curved stone railing, the Chrysos Heir of Worldbearing steadied a scroll against his knee, quill scratching out supply routes and reconstruction plans, focused solely on doing anything that didn’t make his chest twist the way certain things (or certain princes) did. 

Then familiar footsteps approached, firm and impossible to ignore.

“Busy as always,” Mydei drawled, stepping into view with the infuriating ease of someone who definitely had ulterior motives behind seemingly unpretentious words. He carried a bowl in one hand, and from where Phainon was, he could assume from the glimmered shards of crimson under the light, that was Pomegranate. It would be cute how much Mydei loved the fruit to the point he actually strolled around carrying a bowl full of them. But knowing him? There was no trace of good intentions there, only trouble for his heart!

Phainon’s jaw tightened. His eyes snapped back to the parchment,clutching it like it could somehow make him invisible, the desperation of the situation making him pray for any Titan out there that this time, he wouldn't be the star of another foolish spectacle a second time. Especially in front of the damn Kremnoan prince.

Mydei, naturally, ignored the dismissal. He slipped onto the same stone pillar Phainon was perched on, the warmth of his presence bleeding through the narrow space between them. A seed glinted between the prince’s fingers before he slipped it past his lips, slowly , as if he wanted Phainon to witness every second of it.

The silver haired man caught the motion in the corner of his eye and cursed silently. The smear of red across Mydei’s lips was already obscene enough the last time. Now—now he was deliberately rolling the fruit against his tongue, letting juice stain the corner of his mouth. He wasn’t sure if it was pomegranate or punishment.

“Do you ever rest, Deliverer?” Mydei asked, voice rich and casual. His lips glistened faintly as he licked away the juice. “Or do you think peace means working yourself into an early grave?”

“I rest when necessary,” Phainon replied shortly, trying to focus on the neat lines of his ink and not the shape of Mydei’s mouth. “Besides, reprieve won’t carry your people for you, Prince Mydeimos.” His words were steady, but every cell on his body tensed at Mydei’s nearness despite the soft warmth emanating off him, almost too comfortable to resist.

A low chuckle rumbled from Mydei’s chest. “It also doesn’t mean you’re not here for them. Your stubbornness won’t lead you anywhere.” Another seed disappeared between his lips as his tongue flicked out again, slowly dragging along the pad of his thumb to catch the spill of juice and the tiny, wet sound of it nearly tore through Phainon's composure.

Titan’s breath, he was doing it on purpose.

“Do you have to be so noisy?” Phainon muttered, forcing himself to draw another line across the parchment, hands trembling only slightly, because he wouldn't break that easily.

Myde gave him a cute head tilt, usually used when he was confused, but in this case, it was a feigning innocence. “Noisy?” He sucked another seed into his mouth, lips closing around his finger just a little too long. “I didn’t realize fruit offended your delicate sensibilities.”

Phainon ground his teeth. “It doesn’t.”

An insufferable smirk made its way to the golden haired man’s lips as he whispered into the other’s ear, voice low. “Then why won’t you look at me properly, Deliverer?”

A hot, stupid blush surged up his neck. Why was this man so unfair? The only thing he could do was to hold onto his quill for his dear life, only to realize a little too late the loud crack under his grip. Ink bled across the page in a crooked blot, spreading too fast. He swore, pressing his hand down to contain it, but in his haste his sleeve dragged through the mess, fabric soaking black. The stain crept wider, unstoppable, just like the heat clawing up his chest.

Worst of all? He didn’t even care. All he could think of was him.

His heart screamed for his body to move, to grab that smug jaw and wipe the arrogance from it with his mouth until the mighty prince of Kremnos forgot his own name. He wanted that so much, it was nearly unbearable. But all he did was clutch the ruined quill, making it bent slightly, the ink oozing even more through his fingers.

Already sensing that his next humiliation was near, he crumpled the mess and the broken quill together and stood abruptly. “You’re impossible sometimes.”

Mydei, who was watching the whole scene unfold before his eyes, chuckled perfectly unbothered. “You say that often,” he said lazily. “And yet you’re still here.”

Phainon turned sharply, cloak whipping around him, determined to walk away before he did something catastrophic. But then Mydei gave a deliberate, wet slurp as he sucked the last trace of pomegranate from his thumb.

“Did you know,” Mydei said lightly, voice like steel wrapped in silk, “that in some old stories, pomegranates were symbols of temptation? That one taste could bind you forever?” He rolled the final seed between his teeth, letting crimson stain his tongue before swallowing. “I wonder if you’d survive a bite.”

Phainon turned, eyes blazing despite himself. “Do you enjoy tormenting me?”

The heir’s grin widened, slow and devastating. “Immensely.”

For one breathless instant, neither of them moved. Phainon’s body burned with their proximity, his blood singing rebellion against the discipline that had ruled him for so long.

But he didn’t.

Not now. Not yet.

So he inhaled, deep and sharp, and forced steel into his voice. “Childish.”

Mydei laughed unrepentantly, the sound echoing off the marble walls. “If that’s what you want to call it, Deliverer. But you looked.” He tipped the empty bowl toward him in mock salute. “And you wanted.”

Phainon’s silence betrayed him more than words ever could.

He turned on his heel before Mydei could twist the knife further, heart slamming on his chest.

“Next time,” Mydei called after him, the teasing already on the tip of his tongue, “why not have a bite?”

The words followed him down the corridor, searing themselves deep into his mind long after the sound had faded. He forced his legs to move, each step heavier than the last, clinging to the fragile illusion that he could ignore Mydei’s presence. It was a necessity at this point. But, of course, he couldn’t. Of course not. How could he ever turn away from his kindred spirit?

The next strike came on a night like any other. Phainon had just returned from a mission in the lower districts, with scuffed armor and an aching body, but nonetheless satisfied with the results. The task was done and the people safe, no more black tide in sight. It was well past midnight, already curtain-fall hours, when the world softened into darkness.

He was so tired, the soreness of his body already present. Every step pushed him closer and closer to the baths, the number one place he wanted to be at the moment, considering Mydei’s arms were permanently out of the question.

That was until he turned the corner and his stomach flipped like a banner in the wind.

Right there, in front of the bath entrance, was him—the most beautiful face in Okhema (his own words, not anyone else’s), and the reason for far too many of his sleepless nights. Mydei stood there with his arms folded, posture regal and careless all at once. His golden hair caught the dim light like liquid bronze, reflecting what little glow remained in the darkness, while his tattoos lay half-hidden beneath loose robes that hung low on his shoulders, taunting a certain blue eyed gaze just a little.

Phainon slowed his steps, heart skipping a beat. “You waited for me?” he blurted out, not being capable of containing the smile that broke across his face, unguarded and bright, almost foolish. He only realized it once it had already escaped.

“Of course.” Mydei’s answer was simple, his tone maddeningly soft. “You drag me here so often at this hour that now I get restless when you don’t.”

The Kremnoan prince's honesty was well known around Okhema, even if he held back sometimes depending on the person. But with Phainon? He was usually a creature full of blunt truths and pointed jabs. That’s why something in the way he spoke didn't feel like their normal.  There was an unexpected, vulnerable softness in his eyes.

“I —” The silver haired cleared his throat, forcing a calmness he definitely didn’t feel. “— didn’t think you’d notice.”

Mydei tipped his head, that troublesome smirk appearing again. “I notice plenty, Deliverer.”

Phainon swallowed, his throat suddenly dry, and like the mighty deliverer that he was, ended up choking on his own saliva. Great.

He pushed himself to move, slipping past the other heir and into the fog of the baths. Trying to ignore the weight of Mydei’s amused stare trailing after him.

The air inside was thick and hot, a faint scent of mineral stone and herbs filled the room. He removed his armor piece by piece, placing it on the floor carefully, while trying to collect all his thoughts that were all over the place. He could feel Mydei’s presence just beyond the divider, a distracting thing, burning hotter than the damn baths themselves.

Of course, it didn’t take long before Mydei followed him.

The prince walked in with a careless roll of his shoulders. His robe slipped off his arms in one smooth motion, being way too smooth to be unplanned, as it landed carelessly on the floor. He didn't even glance at it, just stepped into the water and sat down, like it was his personal throne.

Phainon tried to force his eyes anywhere where there wasn’t skin involved ,, staring at the ripples of water like they were the most fascinating thing in existence.

But the other heir wasn’t about to let him off so easily.

“So,” Mydei began, wading closer, water lapping at the ink curling around his chest. “How was the mission?”

“Efficient,” Phainon said quickly, too quickly for his own liking. “Handled without issues.”

“Mm. Good.” Mydei leaned back against the edge of the pool, stretching his arms across the rim. The pose was indecently relaxed, his body gleaming in the steam, muscles etched in bronze and shadow. “I was almost worried, you being late.”

Phainon’s head snapped toward him before he could stop it. “Worried?”

Mydei’s smirk deepened. “I said almost.”

Phainon exhaled hard through his nose, sinking deeper into the water to hide the tension on his shoulders. This was unbearable. Every word Mydei spoke, every movement, every glance, was all a calculated trap designed to make him lose his mind.

And worst of all? It was working. Of course it was, because Phainon couldn’t keep his feelings in check.

Silence weighed on them, as the mist clung heavily to their damp skin. Mydei lifted a hand, dragging wet fingers through his hair, pushing it back. Water slid over his neck and chest, droplets following the inked lines across his taut skin in slow motion.

Phainon tried, for a damn long second, he really tried to look away. But his eyes slipped anyway. They’ve been slipping a lot lately.

Could he really be blamed for staring?

Mydei laughed softly. It wasn’t cruel, at least, not entirely. It was low, knowing, like a prince who had just confirmed his victory in a game Phainon hadn’t realized he was playing.

“You make it too easy, Deliverer.”

“And what exactly do you mean by that?” A flicker of warmth rose to his cheeks immediately, not knowing if it was the heat already getting to his brain or the need to maintain the little dignity he had left. “ I’ll let you know that I’m pretty complex!”

The retort didn’t work, because what Phainon received instead was a cute — cute!—fond smile. Mydei’s eyes shined so brightly in the dim light, why was every aspect of that man so dreamy? Then, the prince leaned forward and rested his elbows on his knees. "I mean that for someone who is selfless and restrained, you are terrible at hiding when you want something."

The words sliced clean through him. The urge to argue only grew, even if his only desire was to rise from the water and storm out. But he did neither, because his body betrayed him. Too limp with the hot water to run, and mind too fogged to retort, so he stayed put, eyes unable to meet the other’s.

Seeing that no response was coming, the tattooed man just leaned back against the rim of the pool and closed his eyes, lips stretching like a lion savoring the chase.

Phainon remained motionless, his heart caught between fury and longing.

And just like that, another mark was etched into him, one more battle lost, another invisible wound left behind by Mydei’s relentless, teasing assault.

The evening sun was brutal. It sat low, turning the walls and stones of the training grounds a blinding and angry orange. The heat stuck to everything around and the air barely moved, trembling just from the unbearable proximity of the two demigods circling each other, wooden blades in hand.

Mydei’s tattoos gleamed faintly, the red fiery lines traced in sweat along his arms. His body moved with a beautiful ease, all sharp grace and unreserved confidence. And that grin. Titans save him, that grin. It was a punch to Phainon’s gut and an invitation all at once. 

“You’re slow today, Deliverer.” he rolled his shoulders as if this were no more than a child’s play. “Or have you finally grown tired of losing to me?”

Phainon’s grip tightened on his weapon. “First of all, we are tied. And second, I never tire.”

“Then what is it?” the prince lunged, their blades clashing with a crack that rang through the air, causing sparks to shoot up Phainon’s arms. “Distracted?”

The blue eyed heir grounded his teeth, forcing himself to meet the strike, pushing back with practiced precision. Oh he was distracted, alright. The way Mydei kept watching him, like he had Phainon already figured out, made his control on the verge of falling apart. And all thanks to this one beautiful idiot.

The only thing he could do was shove against the other, a sudden, clumsy attempt to break the hold Mydei had created, but as he swung his sword, the blade only cut through air. He spat back some bitter words, because he felt like it and because he was feeling petty. “Your arrogance will be your downfall.”

“And your restraint will be yours.” The Kremnoan’s voice curled like smoke, low and taunting. He darted in again swiftly, forcing Phainon to parry. Their bodies slammed close,  far too close for comfort, muscles straining against one another.

The silver-haired heir forced a breath, struggling to steady his rhythm. This was a normal spar, the same kind they’d shared since the day they met. Nothing more. He could not let Mydei win, not this fight and even less the one raging inside him.

But the prince clearly had other ideas.

Mydei feinted and twisted, locking their blades together again, faces only inches apart. His grin was sharp, dangerous. “You’re still holding back. I can feel it.”

“I am not.”

“You are.” His tone dropped, deliberate. “You always are, Deliverer.”

One wrong move, and everything he’d buried for cycles would come spilling out. So instead, he threw his frustrations at the other heir, like the mature person he was. “Do you enjoy this?”

Mydei’s smile curved slowly. “Enjoy what?”

“This.” The silver-haired heir pressed in, trying very hard to look composed for someone one breath away from losing it all entirely. “Making me want. Watching me crawl inside my own damn skin because I can’t—” He cut himself off, breath ripping from his lungs.

“That’s all I have left, Mydei. Restraint. I don’t think I’m worthy of anything anymore.”

With all his strength, Mydei pushed against the lock of their weapons, forcing Phainon back until his shoulders hit the nearest wall. “All I’m hearing are excuses.” His voice was firm, breath warm against the other’s ear. “You don’t need that with me.”

Mydei pressed even closer, trying to merge their bodies even though the fabric of Phainon’s clothes. “What is it you’re so terrified of? Say it.” The prince asked, watching him closely.

Terrified? He’d faced Titans, endured excruciating loneliness without flinching, and nearly lost himself in the process. He had carried the world on his shoulders thirty-three million times, never once looking back in doubt of what he needed to do. But this—this heir, this relentless prince, this unspoken thing between them—was what truly terrified him.

Because he wanted. He wanted so much it was unbearable.

Watching Phainon’s inner turmoil, Mydei inched closer, letting his gaze sweep over every tense line of the other’s body. His voice came as a whisper of victory. “Don’t hold back.”

It wasn’t permission. It was a challenge.

And Phainon had never walked away from those.

A grunt tore from the deepest parts of his soul as he threw his sword aside, not giving a care in the world to where it landed. He wasn’t thinking properly anymore, that much was certain. In one sharp, reckless motion, Phainon spun them, driving Mydei against the wall hard enough to make the stone tremble. He couldn’t take it anymore! Every second without the prince’s mouth on his own was pure agony. To fix that, he yanked Mydei by his golden collar, pulling him close until their lips collided in a bruising, desperate kiss.

The world fell silent. No battlefield, no cycles, no evil schemes. Only the searing heat of Mydei’s soft lips against his, the taste of salt and sweat and something far sweeter beneath. It was clumsy and raw, something undeniably theirs. Titans — it was really happening, and Phainon might not survive.

Mydei stilled just for a moment, then let out a triumphant laugh into the kiss, locking the silver-haired heir into an embrace. Every desperate push was met with equal force, teeth grazing, lips tangling, leaving him dizzy and undone.

Phainon's hands trembled as they continued clutching the heavy necklace, afraid everything would disappear if he let go. But it didn’t matter anymore. The prince’s taste was already engraved onto his tongue either way and all he could do now was to surrender. Honestly, not the worst fate — letting himself drown in the love that had haunted him for an eternity.

When they finally broke apart, lungs screaming for air, Phainon pressed their foreheads together, letting the heat of the moment settle between them. By the Titans, he really needed a minute to gather his thoughts. “I can’t — ” He drew in a shaky breath that didn’t help. “I can’t keep pretending, Mydei.”

And Mydei, beautiful and merciless Mydei, for the first time since they started their friendly spar, gave him that soft, nearly-there smile that meant Phainon was doing something right. “Finally,” his thumb slid along the heir’s jaw, slowly, lingering long enough to make the air between them feel electric. His eyes gleamed with satisfaction, a trace of something softer buried beneath — relief, perhaps? “Do you have any idea how long I’ve been waiting for you to snap?”

“You’ve been playing with me.” Phainon tried to scowl, really tried, but the expression crumbled halfway, giving place to an amused smile.

“And you’ve been pretending you don’t want this. Guess we both ran out of lies.”

The silver-haired man finally let go of the necklace, settling his hands on the prince’s hips. A faint pout curved his lips. “You’re insufferable, did you know that?” he murmured, voice edged with warmth. “Did you know that?”

“And yet,” Mydei said, leaning in again, nearly touching, a promise and a threat all at once. “You kissed me.”

Phainon swallowed hard, his whole body trembling under the weight of what he’d done. Finally, he’d let himself want.

And Titans help him, he didn’t regret any second of it.

His hands lifted, cradling Mydei’s face. “Yes, I did. And I’ll do it again,” he murmured, pressing quick kisses to his cheeks. “And again.” One to his jaw. “And again.” Finally, to his lips, each word spilling out with raw, unguarded feelings. “Again, and again. So you’d better be prepared, Mydeimos. You’re not getting rid of me that easily.”

A low chuckle, “I don’t intend to.”

Phainon’s chest tightened, and he could feel his pulse in his throat. “Good. My heart is officially yours now. Do with it as you see fit.”

Mydei’s gaze softened, just a little. “You know you don’t have to rebuild this world alone. We all share the same hopes, the same grief. And now that we’re finally free from all this duty… let me indulge you.”

Phainon blinked, a small, incredulous laugh escaping him. “So that means you will make it up to me for all the times in those 33,550,337 cycles we didn’t spend kissing?”

Mydei’s eyes narrowed just slightly as he crossed his arms, leaning back with the effortless grace of someone who knew exactly the effect he had on the Deliverer's heart, serenity written all over his face. “Do whatever you want, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.”

Well, who was he to deny the Kremnoan prince of such a request?

Phainon crushed their mouths together, a violent storm of teeth and tongue and eons of starving hunger bleeding through all at once. Mydei gasped into the kiss, laughter tangled with short and sharp grunts, as his hands flew to the back of Phainon’s neck. The blue eyed heir didn't care about anything anymore. Now that they were finally taking the next steps, not even the Aeons could rip them apart.

Phainon's fingers closed around Mydei's robes, the fabric bunching in his fists, and like the starved man that he was, he had to taste everything at once: the sharp line of a jaw, the irresistible temptation of that throat, the frantic, delicious throb of the other’s pulse hammering beneath soft flesh.

“Titans, Mydei,” Phainon growled, his mouth hot against the prince’s neck, sucking hard enough to intentionally leave a bruise, his teeth grazing the slick on Mydei’s skin. “You drive me fucking insane.”

“Good,” Mydei panted, tilting his head back, offering more of himself. “Then do something about it.”

Phainon didn't need to be asked twice. His hands shifted, one rough tug freeing the Kremnoan from his tunic.It dropped to the ground, leaving Mydei exposed from the waist up, taut muscles and temptation incarnate, all for blue hungry eyes to devour.

His breath came rough and uneven as he leaned in, tracing a desperate path down Mydei’s throat, over the slope of his shoulder, then lower, until his lips found one perfect, flushed nipple.His mouth moved with calculated hunger, each sweep of his tongue a demanding pressure that made the prince convulse and arch his hips.Phainon’s teeth caught the hardened nub in a teasing bite, before soothing it with his tongue, suckling deep until Mydei’s voice cracked, panting curses and broken praises into the dark night.
